subject.title: [Bug]: MidTurnPrecheckSignal leaks error to UI via pushLoopFailure before internal retry completes

question: Should the fix bubble this control-flow signal through reusable agent-core, or keep agent-core generic and route it through an embedded-runner-owned or generic error-bubbling seam?
rationale: Current source proves the leak path, but the open fix candidate hard-codes an OpenClaw embedded-runner sentinel inside reusable agent-core, which prior review flagged as an owner-boundary decision rather than a purely mechanical repair.

options.title: Use an owned or generic bubbling seam
options.body: Preserve agent-core as a reusable package and add a typed/generic control-flow escape path that the embedded runner can use for MidTurnPrecheckSignal.

options.title: Accept agent-core sentinel handling
options.body: Allow agent-core to recognize this OpenClaw-specific signal directly, trading a smaller patch for a tighter package coupling.

options.title: Adopt the open PR after proof
options.body: Ask the author of https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/99435 to add proof and tests after maintainers choose the boundary shape.

recommendation.title: Use an owned or generic bubbling seam
recommendation.body: Preserve agent-core as a reusable package and add a typed/generic control-flow escape path that the embedded runner can use for MidTurnPrecheckSignal.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has adjacent overflow-recovery history and is a plausible owner for the truncation/compaction boundary decision.
